transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rahul Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Kestrel Head of Search), Omar Khan (Kestrel Backend), Priya Singh (Kestrel Data Eng), Evan Park (Product)

Auto-summary (auto gen): Maya kicks off with goals: reduce search latency and improve top-K relevance for product searches. Rahul gives live demo of embeddings + rerank endpoints via hosted API and Console. Discussion covers batching, KV cache, and security requirements.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um I'll hand over to Rahul for the demo in a moment but quick intros — I'm Maya, AE on the account
[00:08] Rahul Patel: hi all, Rahul here, I'm gonna show the hosted API flow for embeddings and the reranker plus how Console + Optimize surfaces perf recommendations
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: great thanks, quick note, our main KPI is click-through at top 3 and tail latency under 120 ms P95, and we try to keep infra costs flat quarter over quarter
[00:30] Omar Khan: also want to emphasize we run in GCP us-west and need to confirm residency and VPC peering options
[00:37] Rahul Patel: yep totally, we'll cover VPC and the private deploy options briefly — for this session we'll demo hosted because it's fastest for POC

[01:02] Rahul Patel: ok starting, here's the typical flow: we call /embeddings endpoint with the search queries and docs vectorize offline, you can use our batch embed API or streaming depending on throughput
[01:18] Speaker 1 (transcription artefact): there's an embeddings model catalog in Console — you can pick a smaller prod model for lower cost
[01:30] Rahul Patel: correct, and then rerank — we send the top-k candidates and the reranker endpoint does a cross-encoder style rerank, that keeps quality high for the top results
[01:45] Priya Singh: quick Q — do you recommend using the reranker for every query or only for long-tail\/ambiguous queries?
[01:52] Rahul Patel: great question, typical pattern is two-stage: embed search to fetch 50, then rerank top 5-10. Redwood Optimize can suggest that threshold based on your QPS and latency SLOs

[03:10] Rahul Patel: demoing live: Console -> Projects -> Kestrel-POC, here's the embeddings route and the rerank route, you can see per-route metrics like avg latency, p95, token counts
[03:30] Rahul Patel: note the console shows batching slider and cache TTL, Optimize suggests a batch size of 8 for your median query length
[03:45] Evan Park: the Optimize suggestions, are those automated or do we need to run a calibration job?
[03:50] Rahul Patel: they are heuristics from runtime telemetry + our model catalog; you can run a quick calibration job with a sample workload for tailored suggestions

[05:00] Rahul Patel: switching to a short recorded sample — calling /v1/embeddings with text payload, response returns 1536-d float vector (or quantized int8 blob for lower cost option) — small notes: our hosted API supports float16 and quantized variants transparently
[05:30] Omar Khan: you said quantized — how much quality drop if we go to int8?
[05:36] Rahul Patel: depends on model, typically 1-2% NDCG for rerank tasks, Optimize will flag models where quantization is recommended; plus we keep model variants for fallbacks

[06:12] Lena Ortiz: security thing — do you store raw user queries? our legal team wants logs off by default and KMS e2e encryption
[06:20] Maya Chen: yes so hosted by default retains short audit logs for troubleshooting but we have opt-out and redaction options; for PII you can enable auto-redaction and we integrate with customer KMS for key management
[06:35] Priya Singh: and SSO? we use Okta and need SAML for console access and RBAC
[06:40] Rahul Patel: SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning supported, RBAC for routes and tokens is in Console and audit events flow to your SIEM

[08:00] Rahul Patel: now the rerank API sample: we send query + top candidates, you get scores and explainability tokens in the response if enabled — note explainability increases response size and slightly latency so it's optional
[08:25] Omar Khan: can we stream rerank responses if we want to show progressive ranking?
[08:30] Rahul Patel: streaming for generation endpoints is supported today; for rerank it's single-shot currently but we are exploring streaming-style partial scoring — not GA

[09:20] Rahul Patel: let's talk perf: for embeddings we use continuous batching and kv cache for prefix reuse. In your workloads, if many queries share prefixes the KV cache cuts cost heavily
[09:36] Lena Ortiz: we've got a lot of product synonyms and common phrase starts — sounds promising
[09:40] Rahul Patel: also smart routing can fall back to a smaller model if you hit capacity; that keeps service up but with slightly different quality-cost tradeoffs

[11:00] Rahul Patel: switching to a small benchmark I ran with an anonymized slice of Kestrel catalog (10k docs) — P50 latency for embed+search around 37ms, rerank top 5 avg 45ms so combined P95 ~108ms in the hosted us-west region for the profile I ran
[11:22] Priya Singh: that's in range of our 120ms P95 target — what's the QPS for that bench?
[11:28] Rahul Patel: bench was simulating 40 QPS sustained with batching enabled; if you want to scale to 200 QPS we'd recommend dedicated capacity or a reserved pool

[12:00] Lena Ortiz: what about cost numbers — do you have a quick per-query token cost?
[12:06] Maya Chen: we'll send the pricing spreadsheet but ballpark for embed + small rerank variant it's X cents per query at 50 candidate fetch, that drops with batching and quantization
[12:20] Omar Khan: is there a cost calculator in Console?
[12:24] Rahul Patel: Console shows per-route token usage and estimated costs, and Optimize will simulate cost delta for proposed config changes

[13:15] Evan Park: about model drift detection — can Optimize alert us if rerank quality changes?
[13:22] Rahul Patel: yes, quality monitoring ties to prompt sets and evals, you can configure regression alerts and tie them to rollbacks or model pinning policies

[14:50] Priya Singh: network/security — VPC peering and private IP endpoints, is that supported on hosted?
[14:58] Maya Chen: we support VPC peering for enterprise plans and Private (VPC/on-prem) if you need full isolation. For hosted POC we can set up IP allowlists and private endpoints depending on region
[15:20] Omar Khan: do you have a SOC2 report? our infosec needs it
[15:24] Maya Chen: yes SOC 2 Type II, and we have ISO docs; I'll share the security pack link after the call

[16:45] Rahul Patel: demoing a small change — toggled rerank explainability and showed Console trace: there's a per-token breakdown, latency waterfall, and token-level cost metric
[17:05] Speaker 2 (auto): transcription artifact — waterfall sometimes shows a k-b cache miss as "k-b cash"
[17:12] Rahul Patel: haha yeah, our transcripts do that sometimes — but it's KV cache, sorry, k-v cache

[18:30] Rahul Patel: now switching to an example of using the /batch-embeddings endpoint — you can send up to 512 items per batch, and Console will visualize throughput; Optimize suggested batch size will balance latency and token-cost
[18:52] Priya Singh: for offline indexing we plan nightly embeds — any tips?
[18:56] Rahul Patel: use batch embeddings with parallel workers, and use our incremental upsert pattern to avoid re-embedding the whole index — Console and the SDKs have helpers for this

[20:10] Lena Ortiz: failure modes — if the reranker fails do you have automatic fallbacks?
[20:15] Rahul Patel: yes fallback policy can route to the embedding-only rank or to a cached result. You configure policies per-route, and you can have canary rollouts to test new versions

[21:40] Omar Khan: curious about tokenization differences and cross-model scoring — if we use different models for embed and rerank does that affect scores?
[21:48] Rahul Patel: cross-model configs are supported but you need to normalize embeddings or use consistent input prep; we document best practices and have a small normalization lib in the SDK

[23:00] Rahul Patel: quick note on observability — Console traces include request id, route, model version, and the sample logs, and you can forward traces to Datadog or your SIEM

[24:10] Priya Singh: can we store our own embeddings in Redwood-managed vector DB or do we push to external store?
[24:18] Rahul Patel: hosted flow stores vectors in our managed store for convenience, but you can also keep vectors in your store and call our rerank endpoint only; we support connectors to common vector DBs

[25:40] Evan Park: regarding GDPR/data residency — we need EU-only processing for a subset of customers
[25:47] Maya Chen: we have region pins and can route requests to EU regions; for strict residency we recommend Private or dedicated hosting in specific regions

[27:10] Rahul Patel: I'm going to run a short live QPS demo — simulating queries and showing how batch size changes affect latency and cost in Console — note how P95 flattens with small batches up to a point and then increases if batches get too large

[30:00] (demo runs with terminal noises, a few keystrokes, brief pause)

[32:05] Rahul Patel: results: with batch size 8 and KV cache on, average token-cost dropped 22% and P95 stayed under target for the simulated workload

[33:12] Lena Ortiz: impressive. For POC we want a real run against data and our infra — we'll provide a 10k sample plus peak QPS numbers
[33:20] Maya Chen: perfect. Rahul, can you run a bench with that sample and share numbers?
[33:25] Rahul Patel: yes I'll run the bench and include both hosted baseline and a dedicated-reserved estimate so you can compare

[34:00] Priya Singh: any caveats for mixing quantized embeddings and full-precision rerank?
[34:06] Rahul Patel: mixing is ok if you test quality; sometimes quantized embed vectors feed the retriever and the reranker uses a full-precision cross-encoder. Optimize flags risky combos

[35:30] Evan Park: who handles support during the POC? we want an SE touchpoint
[35:35] Maya Chen: Rahul will be the primary SE for the POC and you'll have access to our onboarding docs and a dedicated Slack channel for quick syncs

[36:10] Rahul Patel: I'm noting follow-ups: run the bench, share pricing, share security pack, schedule the POC kickoff. Any other must-haves?
[36:22] Omar Khan: please include network diagrams for VPC peering and a sample SAML assertion flow for our infra team

[37:00] Maya Chen: will do — I'll include diagrams and the SOC2 link. Also sending a short quickstart note on how to call embeddings+rerank endpoints from our Python SDK

[38:30] Priya Singh: small nit - do you have rate-limits per API key? we need burst windows for launches
[38:35] Rahul Patel: yes rate limits configurable per key and per-route, and we can set burst allowances and quota-based throttling for traffic spikes

[39:50] Lena Ortiz: timeline-wise we want to run the POC next two weeks and decide by end of May if we move to dedicated
[39:58] Maya Chen: sounds reasonable — we'll align schedules after this call

[41:10] Rahul Patel: ok wrapping up — recap: we'll send pricing spreadsheet, security docs link, run the bench and share results, schedule kickoff. Action items recorded in CRM and in the email follow-up
[41:30] Evan Park: thanks all, good run-through
[41:35] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, appreciate your time
[41:40] (call ends)

Notes & links shared: https://redwood.ai/decks/kestrel-embeddings-rerank-demo, https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-vpc-pack, sample SDK quickstart gist

Errors/Artifacts: occasional transcription mislabels (Speaker 2/1), some product nouns mis-transcribed ("k-b cash" for KV cache, "red wood"), filler words and crosstalk preserved.
